newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends up on commission house, arb buying.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends up on commission house, arb buying.

text.p: CSCE cocoa prices rallied late in the session to end up sharply Tuesday, led by a round of commission house buying, traders said.
Dealers also noted steady arbitrage-linked buying throughout the day, with arbitrage traders taking advantage of a weaker dollar against Sterling to buy New York futures against the London market.

Automatic commission house buy orders were triggered in New York's most-active December contract at $1,390 a tonne and up, traders said. But December stopped short at $1,400, a key psychological resistance level.
December settled at $1,396, up $17, after ranging between $1,400 and $1,374. Second-position March finished $15 higher at $1,426, while the remaining months gained $12 to $16.
Volume was light at an estimated 5,633 lots Tuesday, up from Monday's official tally of 4,153 lots.
Technically, traders said December's next upside target would be a gap the charts between $1,406 and $1,408.

Traders await the official opening of the Ivory Coast cocoa marketing season, which was slated for today, but the government has not yet fixed farm-gate prices and there is talk the opening may be delayed until October 23.

Traders also await the U.S. third quarter grind figures due Friday at 0845 EDT. Industry sources forecasted a rise between three and ten percent compared to the same period last year, with the majority anticipating an increase toward the lower end of the range.
